Ethel Voynich, The Gadfly.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/ethel-voynich/the-gadfly

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Ethel Voynich, the author and writer of the preface, died 1960 (Wikidata Q466068, P570 = 1960-07-27 and 1960-07-28 in the facts file; the year is the same).

First publication of the text used: 1897 (SE colophon: 'The Gadfly was published in 1897 by Ethel Voynich.'). Wikipedia: published in the United States in June 1897 and in Great Britain in September 1897, about three months apart, so not simultaneous within 30 days.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in the United States in June 1897, before 1931, so the US rule settles the country of origin.
- Country of origin (United States): the text was first published in the United States, before 1931, so the US rule settles the country of origin whatever the death year. Voynich died in 1960, and that date does not change the result.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

- SE colophon: published 1897 by Ethel Voynich.
